data.name: AutoStop_Description
data.value: Stops the keep-alive at the specified date and time (the app doesn't exit)

data.name: DataUsage_Since
data.value: Total since {0:yyyy/MM/dd HH:mm} (measured while the keep-alive is running, including traffic from other apps)

data.name: DataUsage_Note
data.value: While the keep-alive is running, the app counts the data sent and received by the network in use (including traffic from other apps)

data.name: Settings_FallbackHint
data.value: Only when the method fails, the app tries once more with this method (using its destination field below), and records a failure only when both fail. This tells apart a problem with one method (such as a destination outage or blocked ICMP) from a dropped connection. Retrying uses more data.

data.name: Settings_IntervalHint
data.value: Interval: 5 to 3600 seconds. Timeout: 500 to 30000 milliseconds (shorter than the interval). If the connection drops, set the interval to about 15 to 30 seconds.

data.name: Settings_TrafficEstimateHint
data.value: This estimates only the keep-alive's own traffic (it varies with the connection and with IPv4 or IPv6). It doesn't include traffic from other apps, name resolution, or retries with the fallback method. "Data limit" counts traffic from other apps too.

data.name: Settings_DataLimitHint
data.value: Stops when the total data usage counted while the keep-alive is running reaches this value (0 means no limit). This includes traffic from other apps. The total keeps adding up across stops and app restarts until you reset it on the Monitor screen.

data.name: Settings_WeeklyStop
data.value: Stop at a set time every week

data.name: Settings_WeeklyStopHint
data.value: Stops the keep-alive at this time on the chosen days (only while it is running). Unlike a scheduled date and time, this isn't cleared when it stops. Start it yourself or with the network-based auto start.

data.name: Settings_ExitOnAutoStop
data.value: Exit the app when it stops automatically

data.name: Settings_ExitOnAutoStopHint
data.value: The app also exits when the keep-alive stops at a scheduled date and time or at the weekly time. It doesn't exit when it stops because of the data limit or a network disconnection.

data.name: Settings_NotifyOnFailure
data.value: Notify when failures continue and when the connection recovers

data.name: Settings_NotifyHint
data.value: When the traffic fails this many times in a row, the app assumes the connection has dropped, shows a notification, and adds a red dot to the tray icon (1 to 100). When it succeeds again, the app notifies you that it has recovered. The red dot appears even if notifications are off.

data.name: Settings_PreventSleep
data.value: Don't sleep while the keep-alive is running

data.name: Settings_PreventSleepHint
data.value: Prevents automatic sleep when the PC is left idle (the screen still turns off). It can't prevent sleep from closing the lid, pressing the power button, and so on. Laptops use more battery.

data.name: Settings_AutoControl
data.value: Start when connected to the specified network and stop when disconnected

data.name: Settings_RefreshNetworksTip
data.value: Gets the list of connected networks again.

data.name: Settings_NetworkHint
data.value: Connect to tethering, and then choose it from the list. Wi-Fi is matched by its network name (SSID), and USB or Bluetooth tethering by the network name shown in Windows (uppercase and lowercase letters are distinguished). The app starts or stops about 5 seconds after the connection changes. If you stop it yourself while connected, it doesn't start automatically until you reconnect.

data.name: Settings_StartOnLaunch
data.value: Start automatically when the app starts

data.name: Settings_LaunchAtLogin
data.value: Start the app when you sign in to Windows

data.name: Settings_Disclaimer
data.value: * This app sends a small amount of traffic at regular intervals to reduce idle disconnections. It can't guarantee that the connection never drops.

data.name: Settings_AboutTip

data.name: Settings_LicensesTip

data.name: Settings_UserGuideTip
data.value: Opens the user guide in your web browser.

data.name: Method_PingDescription
data.value: Uses the least data and doesn't require administrator rights. Fails on networks that block ICMP.

data.name: Method_HttpDescription
data.value: More likely to work behind a proxy or on networks that block ICMP. Uses more data than Ping. Any HTTP response counts as success.

data.name: Method_TcpDescription
data.value: Connects and immediately disconnects. Connections to the port (such as 443) must be allowed.
